about.en:
Social Network Management: management of all SSNN and attention of users and delivery of a monthly report of analysis of behavior of our social networks. Development of communicational materials: writing of all the institutional pieces (digital brochures, project infographics, concept note, etc.), responsible for collecting testimonies of the mission staff, production of audiovisual material that reflect life stories, etc. Providers management: collect stories and create content, coordinate with the audiovisual provider so it is visible on our SSNN. about.en:
The EVER project (European Volunteering for Environment and Resilience) is managed by France Volontaires. This mission will be based at the Espace Volontariat in Cameroon, in connection with the EVER and V-FORETS projects dedicated to forest preservation in Central Africa. Under the supervision of France Volontaires Cameroun, the volunteer will support communication, capitalization and the animation of networks of actors. Main tasks: 1-Communication and visibility of the EVER project: - Contribute to the communication strategy at national level. - Produce content (promotional, audiovisual and institutional media). - Promote the actions of volunteers and partners. 2 - Coordination of networks of players involved in forest preservation: - Identify players and structure their networking. - Develop a leadership and capacity-building approach.

about.en:
Volunteers participate in daily biodiversity walks, documenting local flora and fauna through observations as well as photo, video, and audio recordings while also exploring new trails together with community members. They help process this data by organizing, classifying, and uploading records to a shared Google Drive folder, using digital identification tools to make preliminary species identifications. Together with local youth, volunteers also create social media content that highlights community activities, biodiversity, and cultural traditions. During dialogue circles, community members, the Despierta team, and volunteers exchange experiences and discuss environmental practices. Volunteers support the preparation and delivery of workshops aimed at strengthening community organization and skills. Additionally, they assist with environmental education for children and young people in local schools.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps humanitarian aid volunteering hosted by Fundación VASE Voluntariado para la Ayuda Social del Ecuador in Quito, Ecuador; activity period 26 weeks within 1 February 2027 – 31 August 2027. Themes: social inclusion and migrants and refugees. No fixed deadline: the host recruits on a rolling basis while the placement is open on the portal. Open to young people aged 18–35 resident in 31 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: The volunteers will be housed in a house exclusively for them, with all the facilities, individual rooms (3) shared (3), full bathroom, dining room, kitchen, rest area. Volunteers will have access in the community to buy the products they need for them to cook every day. Regarding transportation, the volunteers can walk or take buses or community cars to go to work. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate. Humanitarian aid placements also include specific pre-deployment training and security briefings.

about.en:
ICYE Brazil invites volunteers to join the CAVAN Project, a Humanitarian Aid ESC initiative. This program offers a 6-month voluntary experience with the Umbúntu social project in a disadvantaged district of Alvorada city. Umbúntu provides a community and cultural space with workshops on topics like edible plant processing, handicrafts, capoeira, percussion, and language teaching. Volunteers will have a hands-on experience in environmentally sustainable practices by participating in farming, permaculture gardening, construction and other manual activities of our project. The main aims are to provide humanitarian aid, raise awareness about climate change and encourage discussions on green alternatives. Join us now!

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps humanitarian aid volunteering hosted by ABIC - ICYE Brasil in Porto Alegre, Brazil; activity period 8 February 2027 – 8 August 2027. Themes: social inclusion. No fixed deadline: the host recruits on a rolling basis while the placement is open on the portal. Open to young people aged 18–35 resident in 31 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: ICYE Brasil will ensure volunteers are hosted safely and comfortably in a shared flat, providing hot and cold water, Wi-Fi, a washing machine, and private and shared spaces. Breakfast and dinner are provided at home on weekdays by themselves, while lunch and snacks are offered by the project. Weekends include all meals at home. Umbúntu’s focus on organic produce allows volunteers to enjoy and prepare healthy food. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate. Humanitarian aid placements also include specific pre-deployment training and security briefings.

about.en:
Join CPMGA, an organization with over 40 years of experience promoting women’s rights and empowerment in El Alto, Bolivia. Through a feminist approach, CPMGA works to address gender-based violence, promote sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), strengthen citizen participation, and support women’s economic empowerment through training and business incubation. The volunteer will support CPMGA’s fundraising and project development efforts for 9 months by identifying funding opportunities, assisting in the preparation of project proposals and concept notes, and contributing to the development of preliminary budgets and donor documentation. The role also includes collecting and systematizing information from women’s and community organizations, participating in meetings with key stakeholders, supporting project design and proposal-writing training activities, and helping develop communication materials to increase the visibility of projects and funding opportunities.

about.en:
Fundación Munasim Kullakita ( Instagram ) operates "Hogar Trampolín" in Bolivia, a specialized center providing comprehensive protection and rights restitution for girls and female adolescents who are survivors of human trafficking and sexual exploitation. The volunteer supports the lead psychologist in the emotional recovery and identity reconstruction of survivors aged 10-17. The mission focuses on three axes: - helping residents recognize themselves as victims to overcome guilt, - empowering them as survivors through resilience, and - fostering the ability to project a constructive future. Daily tasks include conducting psychological evaluations to guide staff interventions and providing individual and group therapeutic support tailored to cognitive development and cultural backgrounds. The volunteer assists in drafting monthly follow-up, monthly, and reintegration reports for legal authorities. A critical active component involves providing emotional containment during legal proceedings.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps humanitarian aid volunteering hosted by Fundacion Munasim Kullakita in El Alto, Bolivia; activity period 1 December 2026 – 30 November 2027. Themes: anti-discrimination and social inclusion. No fixed deadline: the host recruits on a rolling basis while the placement is open on the portal. Open to young people aged 18–35 resident in 31 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: The Foundation manages the rental of a secure apartment in a residential area of La Paz, ensuring basic utilities, internet, and proximity to services like markets and banks. To reach the "Hogar Trampolín" in El Alto, the volunteer will utilize public transportation, including minibuses and the cable car (Teleférico) network. A standard ESC monthly allowance and pocket money are provided to cover food and personal maintenance. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate. Humanitarian aid placements also include specific pre-deployment training and security briefings.

summary.ar: تطوّع مع «Ghana Developing Communities Association LBG» في Tamale، غانا في مجال مكافحة التمييز والإدماج الاجتماعي ضمن الهيئة الأوروبية للتضامن (تطوع في مجال المساعدات الإنسانية). المدة: 40 أسبوعًا خلال الفترة 1 أكتوبر 2026 – 30 نوفمبر 2027؛ آخر موعد للتقديم 15 ديسمبر 2026، مع تغطية السفر والسكن والطعام ومصروف الجيب.

about.en:
For over 35 years, GDCA has focused on providing education and opportunities to vulnerable and marginalized groups. This mission emphasizes youth and women empowerment as a foundation for an equitable society. The volunteer will promote human rights, leadership, and economic independence by helping participants identify resources to become entrepreneurs and active citizens. As a Youth and Women Empowerment Assistant, the volunteer will play a key role in programs centered on education, employability, and well-being. Responsibilities include - engaging and motivating participants, - conducting community outreach, - advocating for social change. - supporting technical and vocational training (while monitoring program success through surveys and reports) Throughout this mission, the volunteer will help foster social cohesion and enhance employability in order to ensure a lasting positive impact on the local community.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps humanitarian aid volunteering hosted by Ghana Developing Communities Association LBG in Tamale, Ghana; activity period 40 weeks within 1 October 2026 – 30 November 2027. Themes: anti-discrimination and social inclusion. Application deadline: 15 December 2026. Open to young people aged 18–35 resident in 31 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: GDCA organizes accommodation as close to the office as possible, typically a self-contained apartment featuring soft furnishings and individual bathroom facilities. Basic kitchen facilities are provided for meal preparation. GDCA covers transport for official duties and project-related travel. However, costs for personal movement and daily food will be borne by the volunteer, managed within the financial framework and monthly allowance provided by the volunteer program agreement. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate. Humanitarian aid placements also include specific pre-deployment training and security briefings.

eligibility.en: Young people aged 18–35 registered on the European Solidarity Corps portal and legally resident in one of: Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, North Macedonia, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Türkiye. Humanitarian aid volunteering is open only to residents of EU member states and associated programme countries. Host's profile: Candidates must be 18 to 35, reside in an eligible country (EU, North Macedonia, Iceland, Liechtenstein, or Turkey), and have completed the compulsory Humanitarian Aid Volunteering training. A degree in Social Work, Gender Studies, or Community Development is preferred. Please note that total EU volunteering duration cannot exceed 12 months. The volunteer should have experience working with youth or women in educational or NGO settings.

about.en:
Mano a Mano is a Peruvian non-governmental organization committed to improving living conditions in vulnerable communities through environmental, social, and urban development initiatives. Since 2007, the organization has built over 6,000m² of parks in Los Jazmines, Vista Alegre, and Cerrito la Libertad, contributing to violence reduction and enhanced community well-being . Throughout this mission, the volunteer will support community engagement and environmental development efforts by: - Documenting best practices for park construction and maintenance through interviews and consultations; - Organizing workshops to assess the impact of green spaces on public safety, food security, and environmental well-being; - Producing an impact report (qualitative/quantitative) on how parks and access roads influence human rights and community life; - Proposing improvements for future interventions; Strengthening partnerships with municipal services for park maintenance; - Participating in construction and education activities.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps humanitarian aid volunteering hosted by Asociacion MANO A MANO PERU in Lima, Peru; activity period 40 weeks within 1 November 2026 – 30 September 2027. Themes: shelter and social inclusion. Application deadline: 31 December 2026. Open to young people aged 18–35 resident in 31 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: The volunteer is offered a room in Volunteer House which is in the same building as the office. Each one have their seperate room, which could be shared depending on availability. Lunch is provided on office days, and a menu is also available in the field. Public transport is used to travel to the site. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate. Humanitarian aid placements also include specific pre-deployment training and security briefings.

The role of the volunteer will be to support MdM’s communications strategy in Bolivia with the aim of strengthening the communications department as a strategy for publicising the achievements and designs of the various campaigns and projects developed within the projects of MdM Bolivia. The volunteer will be able to assist with the implementation and management of the various social media platforms and other media outlets, as well as the production of official newsletters and information for the beneficiary population. Tasks: - Prepare and run workshops in collaboration with the project teams. - Support the teams in managing social media and institutional platforms to strengthen the mission’s digital presence. - Assist with the design and produce videos. - Assist with the design of promotional materials. - Write press releases.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps humanitarian aid volunteering hosted by Asociacion Médicos del Mundo in La Paz, Bolivia; activity period 25 weeks within 14 January 2027 – 12 July 2027. about.en:
Join STARRY in Sumgait, Azerbaijan, and help create new learning opportunities for children and young people! Hosted by Common Sense Youth Organisation (CSYO), this humanitarian volunteering activity supports communities in H.Z. Taghiyev Settlement and the Beton-Zavod area, where access to extracurricular learning can be limited. Volunteers will facilitate English conversation clubs, educational games, creative workshops, storytelling and activities promoting teamwork, leadership and critical thinking. You will also help encourage girls’ participation in education and organise community activities involving women and families. Working alongside local volunteers, teachers and community members, you will share your skills, learn from others and contribute to a more inclusive learning environment. We welcome Turkish citizens ready to commit to at least eight months of meaningful volunteering. Starting dates are flexible.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps humanitarian aid volunteering hosted by "Saglam Dusunce" Gencler Teskilati Ictimai Birliyi in Sumgait, Azerbaijan; activity period 32 weeks within 1 December 2026 – 1 July 2027. Themes: anti-discrimination and social inclusion. No fixed deadline: the host recruits on a rolling basis while the placement is open on the portal. Open to young people aged 18–35 resident in 1 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: Volunteers will stay in shared apartments with other volunteers in Sumgait. Accommodation, food, pocket money, insurance and visa-related support will be provided in accordance with the ESC Humanitarian Aid programme. Round-trip flight tickets will be purchased directly by EPEKA. Local transportation between the accommodation and activity locations will be provided by CSYO. Detailed financial and practical arrangements will be confirmed before departure. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate. Humanitarian aid placements also include specific pre-deployment training and security briefings.

FOR YOUR APPLICATION TO BE CONSIDERED, YOU ARE REQUIRED TO FILL OUT THIS FORM (YOU NEED TO COPY&PASTE THE LINK TO YOUR BROWSER) Application form: Infopack: It Takes a Village is a three-year Humanitarian Aid volunteering programme supporting rural communities through teamwork, solidarity, and local empowerment. Volunteers work with residents on key areas such as water, education, housing, environment, youth and women’s empowerment, helping improve daily life and strengthen resilience. Year 3 starts this March in Vietnam, where 15 volunteers will spend 45 days supporting the community. Our approach is collaborative, working with the community rather than imposing solutions -shifting the journey from “me” to “we”.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps humanitarian aid volunteering hosted by CSDS Vietnam in Thai Hai Village, Vietnam; activity period 15 March 2027 – 28 April 2027. Themes: disaster relief and water and hygiene. Application deadline: 15 January 2027. Open to young people aged 18–35 resident in 31 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: Accommodation: The volunteers will stay in a traditional stilt-house in the village. The entire floor will be communal, the mattresses are situated on the floor divided by curtains for more privacy. Flushing toilets and showers are available. Food: CSDS will take care of the cooking and food requirements. Normally food includes rice, dairy, eggs, vegetables and meat. Since it will be traditional Vietnamese food, there will also be vegetarian and vegan options. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate. Volunteers will work with ASA , an organization providing shelter and educational support to vulnerable children, adolescents and migrant families. Main tasks may include: - Assist educators in organizing daily activities and providing educational support in shelters. - Accompany children and adolescents during therapeutic sessions, under professional supervision. - Support the implementation of recommendations provided by the psychological team. - Design and facilitate workshops on child protection, migration and conflict resolution for residents and staff. - Collaborate with ASA’s technical team to document and systematize its methodologies and good practices. - Contribute to improving humanitarian assistance and support services for migrant families. The mission combines direct support to vulnerable communities with organizational capacity building.

about.en:
STORM C project is looking for 15 volunteers to join a local community project in Namayumba, Uganda where together we will help create a youth vocational education center. The activities include helping local builders during the erection of a training facility as well as setting up a greenhouse/own vegetable garden. The volunteers will learn how to collect and utilize rain water for sanitation and gardening. Parallel to those activities, the volunteers will also engage with children from St. Joseph Primary School in Namayumba as well as in recruiting local unemployed youth with vulnerable background who can join the carpentry, dressmaking and weaving workshops at the UYSTO center. The project is about rural community support and resilience through empowerment of the local youth. We welcome motivated, sociable and energetic volunteers who would like to join an active, intense and dynamic program with immediately visible result and impact.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps humanitarian aid volunteering hosted by Uganda Youth Skills Training Organization in Kampala, Uganda; activity period 27 March 2027 – 25 May 2027. Themes: social inclusion and education and training. Application deadline: 15 November 2026. Open to young people aged 18–35 resident in 30 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: Volunteers will share rooms in a dorm located within the UYSTO vocational center. Rooms are furnished with bunk beds and wardrobes. There is common kitchen, bathrooms, eating and recreation area. Monday to Friday the meals will be prepared at the camp by UYSTO staff. Volunteers will manage their own meals during the weekends, either cooking together or individually. Local markets and supermarkets provide affordable food options. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate. ADRA Zambia is a non-governmental, faith-based humanitarian organization reaching over 20,000 people annually through programs in health, education, agriculture, and economic empowerment. We focus on empowering communities and building their capacity for sustainable self-reliance. We are looking for a Grant Writer to join our Business Development Unit. In this role, you will support the search for funding opportunities and contribute to writing high-quality proposals. You will receive training on ADRA’s methodologies, country strategies, donor priorities, and effective grant writing. The position is based at our Lusaka headquarters, with field visits to Southern, Eastern, Central, Western, and Lusaka provinces. This role is ideal for someone passionate about humanitarian work, with strong writing skills and an interest in development. Previous experience is an asset but not required—training will be provided.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps humanitarian aid volunteering hosted by ADRA Zambia in Lusaka, Zambia; activity period 39 weeks within 1 November 2026 – 31 July 2027. Living and learning: ADRA will provide comfortable, furnished, and secure accommodation for you in Lusaka city. Zambians are friendly, welcoming people, and speak English and Chinyanja. A monthly sum of approx 450€ will be provided for your upkeep (meals and local transportation). You can make your own meals or use the various kinds of restaurants. Transport is by road using commuter taxis and easy access to several shopping malls. You will share transport with the ADRA team while doing your duties. Volunteers contribute to community programmes by organising non-formal learning activities for young migrants, unaccompanied minors and disadvantaged youth, focusing on language learning, digital literacy, life skills, communication and psychosocial support. about.en:
Green Minds Together is a European Solidarity Corps initiative empowering young people through inclusive, sustainable and innovative activities, aligned with the EU Youth Strategy and UN Sustainable Development Goals. The project promotes employability, active citizenship, environmental responsibility and digital skills through international cooperation. It supports marginalised youth through non-formal education and skills development, encourages civic participation and youth-led initiatives, promotes climate action, recycling and community greening, and strengthens digital literacy, storytelling and communication. In Vietnam, GMT aims to equip young people with the skills and knowledge to thrive in a diverse, interconnected world. Activities focus on education, employment, entrepreneurship, creativity, culture and environmental awareness, enabling participants to develop practical skills, explore innovative ideas, exchange cultures and contribute to sustainable community development.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps humanitarian aid volunteering hosted by CSDS Vietnam in Hanoi, Vietnam; activity period 52 weeks within 1 January 2027 – 31 December 2027. Themes: social inclusion and environment and nature. No fixed deadline: the host recruits on a rolling basis while the placement is open on the portal. Open to young people aged 18–35 resident in 31 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: The volunteer will be living in the volunteer house in a twin room (sharing room with one other volunteer, same gender). The volunteer house has free wifi, hot water for showers in the winter and aircon/fans for the summer. The house has a nanny to take care of cleaning and food cooking. Food is provided 3 times a day, 6 days a week. There is a kitchen with basic utensils that the volunteer can use as needed. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate. Humanitarian aid placements also include specific pre-deployment training and security briefings.

about.en:
Green Minds Together is an initiative that promotes inclusion, sustainability, and community engagement. Acción Guambras works to protect the rights and improve the living conditions of vulnerable children and young people in Quito, Ecuador, especially those at risk of child labour, school dropout, and social exclusion. Through its Reference Centres, the organisation provides educational, nutritional, psychosocial, and family support. Volunteers will assist educators and other professionals by helping children with homework, supporting meal distribution, participating in educational workshops, and accompanying children during recreational activities and educational outings. They will also support health campaigns, help maintain clean and safe activity spaces, and propose creative educational and recreational activities. Volunteers will gradually take more initiative according to their skills and interests, always working alongside the local team.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps humanitarian aid volunteering hosted by Fundacion VASE in Quito, Ecuador; activity period 52 weeks within 1 January 2027 – 31 December 2027. Themes: social inclusion and education and training. No fixed deadline: the host recruits on a rolling basis while the placement is open on the portal. Open to young people aged 18–35 resident in 31 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: Volunteers will stay in a shared apartment in La Mena, southern Quito, with three spacious bedrooms, a fully equipped kitchen, a bathroom, a small living room, and access to a shared rooftop terrace. Each volunteer is responsible for buying groceries and preparing meals using their monthly allowance. Supermarkets and shops are nearby. Public transportation, including buses and the metro, is available. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate. Humanitarian aid placements also include specific pre-deployment training and security briefings.

Green Minds Together is an initiative in Kathmandu/Jitpurphedi, focusing on women’s empowerment, disaster resilience, and sustainable agriculture through permaculture. Volunteers will support women’s leadership, digital and financial literacy, entrepreneurship, and community participation through workshops and activities with women’s groups and cooperatives. They will contribute to disaster awareness campaigns, school safety initiatives, evacuation drills, and community preparedness. In sustainable agriculture, volunteers will participate in farming, composting, soil and water conservation, natural pest management, seed saving, and knowledge-sharing with local farmers. Volunteers will collaborate with local communities, schools, farmers, and community organizations, assisting with educational activities, practical initiatives, awareness campaigns, and project documentation. Their work will promote gender equality, environmental sustainability, and community resilience.

about.en:
Kongo Community Development Association (KoCDA) is a community-based organization in West Africa, Ghana, specifically, in Kongo in the Upper East region. The Organization seeks an active individual to help drive the skills of French language, particularly among school children and community members in Kongo/Nabdam. This vacancy is an interesting position in a grassroots organisation in rural Africa, aimed at equipping young students with essential French language skills. The Upper East region of Ghana is bordered by two French West African speaking countries, Burkina Faso and Togo. Nonetheless, French is not promoted to facilitate good neighbourliness, trade and business opportunities. The long term objective is to encourage French in the Nabdam district. It aims to bridge cultural gaps, fostering better understanding and stronger relationships with communities in neighbouring countries. The volunteer is to help increase French awareness among students.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps humanitarian aid volunteering hosted by Kongo Community Development Organisation in Bolgatanga, Ghana; activity period 24 weeks within 4 January 2027 – 4 July 2027. Themes: social inclusion. Application deadline: 30 November 2026. Open to young people aged 18–35 resident in 31 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: Volunteers will be warmly hosted at the NDAHA Guesthouse, where they will have a private, lockable room with their own bathroom and shower for comfort and security. Electricity and running water are reliably available. Volunteers can prepare their own meals using the shared kitchen facilities, including a refrigerator and kitchen cabinets. Fresh, abundant tropical fruits, vegetables, and local produce are easily accessible. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate. Humanitarian aid placements also include specific pre-deployment training and security briefings.

These centers serve as vital community development hubs offering ICT training, climate-smart agriculture, early childhood education, and more. Addressing a critical digital skills gap especially among youth and vulnerable children the project aims to boost employability and resilience by enhancing digital literacy. These skills are essential to unlocking new educational and career opportunities in an area facing growing challenges from climate change.

about.en:
Join Uganda Pioneers Association and Mondo in a rewarding role aimed at transforming education in a rural community school. As a volunteer, you will lead workshops and training sessions to strengthen school management by equipping teachers with innovative practical and theoretical teaching methods. You will support subject teachers across diverse disciplines, raising community awareness on the vital importance of education. Your role also includes sourcing partnerships to enrich the school library with learning materials, organizing and supervising extracurricular activities, and ensuring students enjoy a well-rounded, holistic education. Moreover, you will actively contribute to the success of Mondo’s community projects, supporting both primary and secondary schools through continuous follow-up and engagement.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps humanitarian aid volunteering hosted by Uganda Pioneers Association in Kampala, Uganda; activity period 24 weeks within 4 January 2027 – 3 July 2027. Themes: social inclusion. Application deadline: 30 November 2026. Open to young people aged 18–35 resident in 31 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: Volunteers will stay at Villa Mamu, Mengo, Kampala, a spacious compound with WiFi, warm showers, kitchen facilities for self-catering, and pets to make the stay homely. To immerse more deeply into the local culture, volunteers will spend some days living with a host family near Kikooba School. Other accommodation options can be arranged in Kampala based on safety, convenience, and security considerations. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate. Humanitarian aid placements also include specific pre-deployment training and security briefings.

about.en:
Mondo Estonia is sending a volunteer to Northern Ghana, where communities face persistent poverty and heavy dependence on rain-fed agriculture. Climate change is worsening these challenges through erratic rainfall, drought, rising temperatures, and flooding, with serious effects on farming, water security, livelihoods, and employment. Rural communities therefore need both immediate adaptation measures and long-term resilience-building strategies. The volunteer will support key activities including conducting climate vulnerability assessments, identifying practical intervention options, building local capacity in energy saving, reduce-reuse-repair-recycle practices, food management, income diversification, and sustainable farming using organic inputs, as well as strengthening networking and stakeholder engagement in climate action.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps humanitarian aid volunteering hosted by Ghana Developing Communities Association LBG in Tamale, Ghana; activity period 24 weeks within 4 January 2027 – 3 July 2027. Themes: social inclusion. Application deadline: 30 November 2026. Open to young people aged 18–35 resident in 31 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: GDCA will provide comfortable accommodation near the office. The accommodation has essential utilities such as water, electricity, internet, and satellite TV, as well as basic kitchen facilities for preparing meals. Participants may also choose to buy meals from nearby restaurants or food vendors, though it is advisable to use reputable vendors. For official duties, GDCA will provide transport. Local taxis and tricycles are also readily available. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate. Humanitarian aid placements also include specific pre-deployment training and security briefings.

about.en:
Kampala School for the Physically Handicapped (KSPH) is a Ugandan primary school for children with physical disabilities, founded in 1968 by parents of children with cerebral palsy. Its aim is to educate, rehabilitate, and equip learners for self-reliance and development. The school follows the national curriculum and offers sports, music, dance, drama, spiritual fellowship, and education tours. It also provides vocational training in tailoring, screen printing, crafts, tie and dye, and basic computer skills for children who cannot continue to further education. KSPH has 100 pupils aged 6–18 with disabilities such as cerebral palsy, muscular dystrophy, spina bifida, and polio. It has 13 teachers, 5 trained in special needs education, including 2 disabled former students. Volunteers support classroom learning, extracurriculars, wheelchair repair (voluntary), therapy exercises, teacher training, fundraising, and basic computer teaching.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps humanitarian aid volunteering hosted by Uganda Pioneers Association in Kampala, Uganda; activity period 24 weeks within 4 January 2027 – 3 July 2027. Themes: social inclusion. Application deadline: 30 November 2026. Open to young people aged 18–35 resident in 31 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: Volunteers will stay at Villa Mamu, Mengo, Kampala, a residence with WiFi, a warm shower, a kitchen, and pets. The volunteer shall prepare their own meals and living in own room. Other accommodation options in Kampala can be arranged based on safety and convenience. Local transport mainly consists of boda-bodas (motorcycle taxis). The project is in Kampala and in a walkable distance from Villa Mamu. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate. Humanitarian aid placements also include specific pre-deployment training and security briefings.

about.en:
Have you ever wondered how it is to be a scientist? Do you wish to discover life in a unique international institute? Are you motivated by the protection of nature and a wish to experience a new culture in an exciting and friendly environment? We are currently looking to host 1 European volunteer for 6 or now! The volunteer will work during all the year on differents projects, depending of the needs of the differents teams and on the feeling of the volunteer. He/she will take part of data collecting, field observations (with ornithologists, botanists or ichtyologists…)n take part of data analysis (on computer) under the responsibility of a project leader. If interest, he/she could work with communication team. For example, your focus could be mainly (but not only) on the Eurasian Spoonbill research, a beautiful bird with a distinct spoon shape like bill or working with the "Water" team to study river, marshes and sea connections. More details on www.tourduvalat.org

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by Tour du Valat in Arles, France; activity period 52 weeks within 10 September 2026 – 30 September 2027. During the week you can have lunch in the onsite canteen, where you will try the most delicious French cuisine. You will be allowed to use a car on weekends and for purchase of food in Arles. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
NGO Društvo Eksena carries out three main programmes: Eksena Daily Centre for Children and Youth, Eksena Psychosocial Counselling Programme, and Eksena – Dementia, Hand in Hand. Volunteers may be involved in all three programmes or focus mainly on one programme, depending on their interests, experience and agreement with the hosting organisation. In the Daily Centre, volunteers support children and young people through creative workshops, educational activities, games, sports, homework support and activities that strengthen social skills and inclusion. In the Psychosocial Counselling Programme, volunteers help with preparation of materials, spaces, awareness-raising and community activities. In the Dementia programme, volunteers support workshops and social activities for elderly people, people with dementia and their relatives. Volunteers work only in a supportive role, under the guidance of staff and mentors.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by Drustvo ZA Strpne Odnose Eksena in Šentjur, Slovenia; activity period 52 weeks within 1 November 2026 – 31 December 2027. Themes: education and training. Application deadline: 30 November 2026. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 35 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: You will be accommodated in a flat close to us. You will have your private bedroom and share the kitchen, bathroom and other spaces in the flat/house with other volunteers. As an ESC volunteer, you will receive health insurance, monthly pocket money for food and other expenses. Volunteers have international health insurance and travel to the volunteer location is covered to a certain amount. In addition, the hosting organization will give the volunteers pocket money allowance once a month. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Are you interested in Media Education and Film-making? Are you prepared to share your skills with other people? It is expected that volunteers produce at least two short videos per month, connected with actual socio-cultural processes. Monthly productions results in "Youth Magazine" which is presented online. Some of them also on different film festivals. If you are interested in media education, you could improve your practical skills while co-mentoring in series of workshops and trainings for local youngsters. DZMP office is equipped with computers, as well as all needed for fieldwork and shooting process. Here you can improve your skills of directing, camerawork, lighting and post-production. Volunteers are provided with the accommodation, money for food & local transportation, pocket money. Travel costs are partly refunded according to the rules of European Solidarity Corps. More info at:

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by Društvo Zaveznikov Mehkega Pristanka in Krško, Slovenia; activity period 52 weeks within 20 February 2027 – 19 February 2028. Themes: culture and creativity and education and training. No fixed deadline: the host recruits on a rolling basis while the placement is open on the portal. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 35 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: The volunteer will live in the house with the other ESC volunteers. She/he will have a private room. The kitchen and bathroom are shared. Volunteers are also responsible for the cleaning of their rooms and shared rooms (kitchen, bathroom and corridor). Smoking in the apartment is not allowed. The volunteers have a possibility to prepare their food in the kitchen (equipped with cooker, oven, fridge...) or to eat in the restaurants. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
This volunteering opportunity within the European Solidarity Corps takes place in the western part of the Czech Republic, specifically in the municipalities of Spálené Poříčí, Žinkovy, and Měcholupy, all located within 30 minutes of the regional capital Plzeň. The activities are carried out within the framework of the Local Action Group of St. John of Nepomuk (MAS SJN) and focus on the cultural and social revitalization of rural areas. Due to their geographic remoteness and low population density, the municipalities in this region often lack sufficient facilities for community activities, which are key to strengthening interpersonal relationships and developing local society. more on link:

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by Místní akční skupina svatého Jana z Nepomuku, z.s. in Spálené Poříčí, Czechia; activity period 1 October 2026 – 30 September 2027. Themes: social inclusion and education and training. Application deadline: 15 April 2027. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 28 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: Accommodation is provided and fully covered by the project. There is a private room on the organization’s premises, equipped with a bathroom and a kitchen. The volunteer will receive pocket money of EUR 7 per day. Travel costs to and from the Czech Republic will be reimbursed according to ESC limits. The volunteer will be accommodated directly in Spálené Poříčí, so there is no need for long daily commuting. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Planet Citizens teaches foreign languages through physical activity in kindergarten and primary schools located in disadvantaged neighbourhoods north of Paris. With our method, APL (Physical and Linguistic Activities), kids learn by moving, playing and speaking. Working with other volunteers and alongside class teachers and educators, you will: - prepare and lead active English (or German) sessions for children aged 3 to 11; - give children and teenagers a positive first contact with other languages, foreign cultures, European citizenship and international mobility; - contribute to the development of our pedagogical method and digital tools; - take part in local community activities (public libraries, neighbourhood and social centres, homework support, holidays camp). You will join a team of six European volunteers. Mission from 1 March to 31 August 2027.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by Planet Citizens - Language Training 2024 in Aubervilliers, France; activity period 26 weeks within 1 March 2027 – 31 August 2027. Themes: citizenship and participation and education and training. No fixed deadline: the host recruits on a rolling basis while the placement is open on the portal. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 32 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: You will share a furnished flat in Saint-Denis with two other European volunteers.The rent is fully covered by Planet Citizens. You will receive a monthly public transport pass valid in the whole Paris region, and a bike for short trips . 467€/month of mission (pocket money and allowance for food and daily costs) + Money to recharge the monthly transportation pass. Your round‑trip to Paris will be reimbursed based on distance. Extra support available for Green Travel. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
You will spend your days with children in primary school (1st graders) and during school break with children in kindergarten (children aged 4-6), every day while parents are at work. Together with 2 teachers in your daily routine you will assist during the regular class hours and help lead sports, language, math, social and nature science, music, design lessons, and in kindergarten also assist play-time in and out-doors, organize visits to other institutions to expand horizon of kids, organize activities for staff, etc. You are invited to be active and come up with Your own creative ideas and develop little concepts of play and projects of Your own initiative. Children of this kindergarten and primary school have special needs and some have disabilities. Valmiera city with nearly 30’000 inhabitants is the economic center of Valmiera county and one of the major cities in Northern Latvia. While it is not too big in European context, it provides all services one might need.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by Valmieras novada pasvaldibas Valmieras Gaujas krasta vidusskola attistibas centrs in Valmiera, Latvia; activity period 25 weeks within 1 January 2027 – 30 June 2027. Themes: education and training and health and wellbeing. No fixed deadline: the host recruits on a rolling basis while the placement is open on the portal. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 30 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: Accommodation is provided in a rental apartment in the center of Valmiera, shared with other volunteers (can be two same-gender persons per room). Each volunteer is provided with a Latvian phone number and a fast internet plan. A city bus card is provided based on actual needs. Food allowance of €7 per day is provided for meals or groceries. In addition, the kindergarten and Gaujas Krasta School provide one hot lunch daily for their staff. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

This paid volunteering project runs from December 2026 to February 2027 and is open to individuals aged 18-30 who are eager to contribute to sustainable farming, conservation, and community initiatives for 3 months! 📌 Location: Kampia, Cyprus 📅 Duration: December 2026 to February 2027 💡 Volunteer Tasks Include: Designing and implementing educational workshops. Your task will be helping in leisure and educational centre for children, young people and families. It is located in smaller town in eastern Bohemia. about.en:
Become a volunteer at the Effatha Socio-Therapeutic Workshop in Krnov, where adults with mental and multiple disabilities engage in activities to develop work habits and social skills, fostering greater independence. Activities: Volunteers will support participants in creating items like gifts, decorative pieces, and ceramics. You'll assist in therapeutic sessions focused on pottery, encaustic art, candle-making, soap-making, and textile projects. Additionally, you'll accompany users during gardening, cooking, memory training, and relaxation exercises. Your responsibilities include preparing materials and workspaces, scheduling activities, and collaborating with social workers. Join us in making a difference! For more information about the project, visit our website at www.intervia.cz.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by Slezská diakonie in Krnov, Czechia; activity period 15 January 2027 – 31 August 2027. Themes: health and wellbeing and education and training. Application deadline: 15 November 2026. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 30 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: 💸 Volunteer with us – Costs Covered! Thanks to the European Solidarity Corps, most of your expenses are sorted: - Private bedroom in a shared flat 🛏️ - Food allowance: 4200 CZK (~170 EUR)/month 🍽️ - Pocket money: 7 EUR/day 💰 - Travel covered: Flights & daily commute ✈️🚗 - Only pay for your own free-time activities 🎨🎢 Focus on the adventure, the experience, and making a real difference! 🌟 As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Accueil Famenne is a non profit organisation whose social aim is to welcome, accompany and support people whose basic needs are barely or not met, without any distinction of origins or believes. It aims to promote fraternity, solidarity, equality and social justice in Rochefort and surroundings. Accueil Famenne has three main axis: – A hosting venue “L’élan“ for single-parent families and isolated and financially disadvantaged people – A food bank for people of Rochefort and surrounding facing financial difficulties – A second hand shop “Li Gurnî“ working according to circular economy principles; providing affordable house items, whose benefits goes to financially support to two first axis. Accueil Famenne works with economically disadvantaged and/or morally isolated people. It adresses its first activity to any adult and family in Brussels and Wallonia, while the food bank is destined to people from Rochefort and surroundings.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by Accueil Famenne in Rochefort, Belgium; activity period 1 February 2027 – 31 January 2028. Themes: anti-discrimination and environment and nature. Application deadline: 8 November 2026. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 29 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: The volunteers will have a private room in a fully-equipped shared house in the city of Rochefort with other ESC volunteers (Depending on which house you live, you’ll be 250 or 650m away). Food: the volunteer will receive a budget and will take care of the meals by themself. Participation in the ESC is free of charge for the participant, except for exceptional contribution to travel costs. The volunteer will receive free board and lodging during the whole activity. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Volunteers of Sininauhasäätiö have a priceless value in our homeless´ people's everyday life by giving their unconditional love and time. Do you want to help the unfortunate ones, while gaining essential work experience and new contacts to your network? Join Sininauhasäätiö´s volunteers. The Blue Ribbon Foundation in Helsinki is an expert and influencer in the field of homelessness and substance abuse work. We develop low-threshold operating models and integrate them into our customers’ everyday lives. We work to make a place for everyone. Our project’s aim is to help and support people who are in the most vulnerable positions in society. We offer two different volunteer profiles so you can choose the role that best matches your interests and skills: Practical ( for 3 volunteers) and Office volunteering (for 1 volunteer).

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by Blue Ribbon Foundation in Helsinki, Finland; activity period 15 January 2027 – 30 September 2027. Themes: social inclusion. Application deadline: 30 November 2026. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 29 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: As a volunteer at The Blue Ribbon Foundation, you live in an apartment in Helsinki. For 6 months, you will be sharing a room with a fellow ESC volunteer, and for the rest, you will have your own room. All volunteers will receive their own HSL card for zones A and B, which lets them access all necessary locations for work and the apartment by public transportation. Pocket money will be 7 euros per day, which will be transferred to your bank account once per month. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Since 2005, Social Action has been dedicated to making a real difference in the lives of young people. We empower youth through exciting quality volunteering opportunities with ESC, impactful international projects (including dynamic Erasmus+ youth exchanges), and essential social services delivered right on the streets. We're currently looking for a passionate volunteer to join our team. You'll connect directly with youth on the streets, playing games, engaging in conversations, inviting them to an open youth evening at our office, and helping with the outings/camps (come rain, snow or sunshine). You'll also boost our digital outreach, ensuring our message reaches a wider audience, and promote exciting European Solidarity Corps opportunities at youth events. We encourage your initiative: cultivate a personal project and contribute to our organisational goals. Come make a real difference with us!

about.en:
The Laboratorio Manodopera Socio-Occupational Center is a vibrant and inclusive space where adults with disabilities explore their potential and develop new skills. Up to 25 participants engage daily in hands-on craft workshops (favors, felt items, artistic packaging), music and expressive labs, motor and aquatic activities, and social-emotional exercises. Structured routines promote autonomy, well-being, and self-confidence. Through collaborations with schools, social centers, and local associations, participants connect with the wider community. Volunteers will experience a dynamic, supportive environment, witnessing creativity, inclusion, and personal growth in action. This is a unique opportunity to learn about social inclusion, educational methodologies, and community engagement while observing and supporting the transformative impact of empowerment, creativity, and skill-building on each participant’s life.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by Campi d'arte Società Cooperativa Sociale in San Pietro in Casale, Italy; activity period 37 weeks within 23 November 2026 – 6 August 2027. Themes: social inclusion and education and training. No fixed deadline: the host recruits on a rolling basis while the placement is open on the portal. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 28 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: Volunteers will live in a nearby town, in a shared apartment with 1–2 others, within a complex hosting 6–7 volunteers involved in different activities across local facilities. Food and accommodation are provided by the organisation, and transport to and from activities is included in the schedule. The accommodation is well connected to the activity locations by public bus, with a bus stop just a few minutes’ walk away. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Solidarités Jeunesses (SJ) is a national movement of non-formal education and is composed of a National Secretary (Paris), and eight regional delegations across France. Our delegations host international volunteers throughout the year. All of the activities organized benefit the local community and share common ground: - gather people from different culture and social background to participate in social, ecological and cultural development. - contribute to the integration of people with fewer opportunities. Each project is dedicated to actions of solidarity and collective living. We believe that cultural exchanges are a key for personal learning and for the volunteer to experiment and undergo personal development. You will find all the information about our available projects and application process in this page :

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by Maison des Bateleurs - Solidarités Jeunesses in Montendre, France; activity period 52 weeks within 1 December 2026 – 30 November 2027. Themes: social inclusion and citizenship and participation. No fixed deadline: the host recruits on a rolling basis while the placement is open on the portal. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 29 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: La Maison des Bateleurs is located in MONTENDRE, in Poitou-Charentes, in the west of France. The site includes a big main house with outbuilding, a vegetable garden, and also a bamboo forest ! It‘s situated close to a golf club in the outskirts of the village, 10 minutes away from the train station. As a volunteer you will share a house with other volunteers! As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
We are looking for 3 young people, who will become part of the volunteering, educational and promotional team in our organization. During the project, volunteers will be helping us with organizing the volunteering, educational and promotional activities in our office. The ESC volunteers will be trained to lead an international volunteer camp - workcamp (2weeks) in Slovakia during summer. They will choose which camp they want to lead: free time activities for seniors, for kids, be part of eco village, reconstruction of castles. They will learn soft skills like leadership, conflict resolution, time management, public speaking, and management of the budget. They will be: * Part of our community * Organising meetings/activities for young people on various topics * Creating educational workshops according to their own initiative and interest, * Promoting volunteering and study themes at schools, *Promoting volunteering and ESC life on social media * Administrative/Office work and many more.

The flat is situated in a convenient area, approximately 30 minutes’ walk from the city centre, with shops, public transport and other important institutions nearby. The accommodation includes laundry facilities and a fully equipped kitchen. Each volunteer will have their own private room. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Only applications made in this form will be considered. DO NOT APPLY VIA THE YOUTH PORTAL! Green Skills integrates the participants into an international community and facilitates their taking part in civil society and grassroots initiatives. It seeks to address societal issues such as climate change and social discrimination through youth empowerment and competence building. Our main objective relates to environmental challenges that we face globally, as well as to the need for resilience; socially, politically, and environmentally. Through events like workshops, presentations, or documentary screenings, people at Suderbyn have many chances to become more informed about the complexities of environmental, political, and social sustainability. The participants contribute to all aspects of running the ecovillage and are organized in 4 separate activity domains, namely: Infrastructure, Permaculture Garden, International projects & networks, Office & Administration.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by Relearn Suderbyn in Visby, Sweden; activity period 17 March 2027 – 17 February 2028. Themes: environment and nature and education and training. Application deadline: 13 November 2026. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 28 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: You will be hosted at Suderbyn ecovillage. Simple accommodation, private rooms, vegan food. The ecovillage is located 9km away from Visby, the main town on the island of Gotland. Gotland is in the middle of the Baltic Sea and part of Sweden. There are daily ferries from Stockholm, capital of Sweden, to the island. You can read more about Suderbyn here: As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

Volunteers will work together with locals to create activities and increase involvement. Volunteers will plan and implement seasonal events (e.g. winter experience, shrovetide, Valentine’s day). They will work at local library as well as participate in the activities of the local youth work: volunteers will work at youth house and arrange fun activities for kids and youngsters. Volunteers will have an opportunity to carry out own ideas. How to apply? During the interview we’ll discuss more about the project. The interviews take place on 24 November 2026.

about.en:
The “Young Leaders” ESC volunteering opportunity takes place in Trnava, Slovakia, organized by Youth for Equality, a non-profit organization focused on education, human rights, and community development. The project aims to support young people in developing soft skills such as communication, teamwork, leadership, and creativity through non-formal education methods like workshops, discussions, and group activities.Volunteers will support activities in schools, organize workshops and events, participate in discussion clubs, and help with community projects. They can also contribute to social media, collaborate with local organizations such as libraries and charities, and even create their own initiatives. The project promotes inclusion by working with diverse groups, including youth, and individuals with fewer opportunities.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by Youth for Equality in Trnava, Slovakia; activity period 46 weeks within 15 January 2027 – 30 October 2027. Themes: education and training and employment and entrepreneurship. No fixed deadline: the host recruits on a rolling basis while the placement is open on the portal. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 28 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: Volunteers will be provided with shared accommodation in apartments in Trnava. Each participant receives a monthly food allowance of 200€ and pocket money of 180€, transferred to their bank account. Travel costs are reimbursed based on the distance between the volunteer’s home country and Slovakia, according to EU rules. Local support and basic living needs are covered, ensuring a comfortable stay during the project. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

The role of the volunteer will always be of support for the professional staff in order to understand the behaviour and attitudes of the 12 people with disability hosted in the house. He/she will help the social workers in recreational and educational group activities and in general in every aspect of everyday life. In particular his/her tasks will be: -support the people with disability in knowing the neighbourhood, the local resources and the community where they live, - organization of moments aimed at developing interpersonal skills with people with disability; - care activities for people with disability -organization of leisure moments aimed at developing guests and volunteers personal hobbies; - collaboration in planning socializing moments.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by Cooperativa Sociale L'Accoglienza in Forlì, Italy; activity period 44 weeks within 15 November 2026 – 15 October 2027. Themes: social inclusion and citizenship and participation. No fixed deadline: the host recruits on a rolling basis while the placement is open on the portal. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 26 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: He/she will live in a flat with other ESC volunteers, the apartment has 5 bedrooms and it’s in the city centre. about.en:
Do you want to help nature get healthy again? We are a non-profit organisation dedicated to create and maintain an eco-friendly way of agriculture. Our gardeners will teach you skills about the nature-friendly production of organic vegetables and fruits, soil regeneration, and nature conservation. Our site is beautifully situated beneath the Eco-Village "Lebensgarten Steyerberg". Enjoy new experiences together with other international volunteers. You will learn a lot about organic gardening and permaculture and dive deeper into innovative practices of creating healthy soil on an organic farm that is certified under the international biocyclic vegan standard. You will gain new green skills, practice-oriented knowledge in organic agriculture and develop your social skills together with our team and in exchange with the inhabitants of the Ecovillage. You can take part in seminars and other activities that will help you to develop your personality and you can make new like minded friends.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by Permakulturpark am Lebensgarten Steyerberg (PaLS) gGmbH in Steyerberg, Germany; activity period 1 February 2027 – 31 January 2028. Themes: food security and environment and nature. Application deadline: 30 November 2026. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 26 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: Accommodation is provided in separate rooms for each participant. Food will be provided by us. A lot of it you will nurture and harvest yourself! Usually the volunteers prepare their meals together in their communal kitchen. Being a farm under the biocyclic vegan standard participants should respect vegan lifestyles. Travel costs at the beginning and end of the service will be reimbursed under conditions set by the ESC-program. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

Make a difference in the life of Estonia's youth in a friendly Estonian School, Youth Center or Kindergarten! Kiviõli is a small community in North-East Estonia that has a local School and Kindergarten. In Kiviõli Kindergarten Kannike the volunteer will assist the teachers with activities and initiate some of his/her activities as well. Kindergarten offers a good opportunity for volunteers to help prepare children for school and in cooperation with parents to carry out a good up-bringing and education for children, taking into consideration specific features of each child, interests and principles of family education. Volunteer's another choice is to take part of activities in a local Maidla School, with a focus on improving school environment and studies. Volunteering duration: January 2027 until June 2027. Dates are flexible. If you are curious, visit our Instagram: instagram.com/noorngo or contact richard@erinoor.ee

about.en:
You 4 Youth is a 10-month volunteering experience in Grottaminarda, supporting Cripta Maynarda in expanding its cultural and social activities. With the help of two volunteers, the project aims to strengthen partnerships and promote volunteering as a tool for community cohesion, solidarity, and active citizenship. Part of You 4 Youth, this initiative encourages young people to take an active role in cultural and social life, fighting social apathy and youth marginalization. 🔹 What’s in it for you? ✔ Promote social inclusion and equal opportunities ✔ Express your creativity and take the lead in activities ✔ Gain valuable personal, social, and professional skills ✔ Get your experience recognized through Youthpass Join us and make a difference while growing as an active European citizen!

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by Cripta Maynarda in Grottaminarda, Italy; activity period 43 weeks within 1 July 2026 – 1 May 2027. Themes: citizenship and participation and education and training. No fixed deadline: the host recruits on a rolling basis while the placement is open on the portal. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 27 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: Volunteers will stay in a shared apartment in the heart of Grottaminarda, fully equipped for a comfortable experience: 🏡 Accommodation details: Each volunteer will have a single bed in a shared double room, along with blankets, two sets of sheets, and a pillow. Personal storage space, including a wardrobe, bedside table, and desk with a lamp. A fully equipped kitchen with a refrigerator, sink, oven, stove, pantry, and all necessary utensils (cutlery, glasses, plates, pots, and pans). As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Our Foundation supports adults with intellectual disabilities. We provide two main services: a Therapy and Work Day Care Centre and supported residential homes. Our key values are normalisation, independence and acceptance. We are looking for open-minded volunteers who treat everyone equally and challenge prejudice. Our project aims to help our clients develop their skills and knowledge through leisure activities. We also organise inclusive programmes with students from the University of Pécs. Here, you will meet wonderful people with intellectual disabilities who have big hearts and are open to others. We have hosted international volunteers before, and our clients are always asking when the next volunteer will arrive. So we are waiting for you! You can join our workshops, spend time with our clients and have fun together!

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by Fogd a Kezem Alapítvány in Pécs, Hungary; activity period 52 weeks within 15 February 2027 – 30 May 2028. Themes: social inclusion and health and wellbeing. Application deadline: 30 March 2027. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 27 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: We rent a two-bedroom apartment with internet access in Pécs, where our volunteers can live. Every month, we provide pocket money and money for food, which volunteers can use to buy food and other things they need. The Foundation also provides household essentials and can help with other needs from time to time. Volunteers receive a Hungarian mobile phone plan with a phone number and internet access. We also provide a monthly bus pass for travelling around the city. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
WE ONLY ACCEPT APPLICATIONS THROUGH OUR FORM: Europa-Haus Leipzig e. V. hosts the official Europe Direct information center for Leipzig Region. Their mission is to bridge the gap between European citizens and EU institutions through civic education, youth exchanges, and public engagement. As a volunteer, you will be an active part of our international team, gaining hands-on experience in European project management, political education, and public communications. You will assist in carrying out the European Commission’s Annual Communication Plan, organize cross-border mobility opportunities (such as Erasmus+), and lead multilingual European city tours throughout Leipzig. This role offers unique opportunities to develop event management skills, travel within Europe for mobility projects and visits (e.g., to the European Commission in Brussels), and learn about local association structures in Leipzig while improving your German language skills.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by VILLA gGmbH in Leipzig, Germany; activity period 1 March 2027 – 29 February 2028. Themes: social inclusion and citizenship and participation. Application deadline: 8 November 2026. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 26 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: You will live together with other volunteers in a shared flat, with your own single bedroom. Furthermore, you will receive food- & pocket money as well as a ticket for public transportation in Leipzig. Check our website for more information about your ESC in Leipzig: As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Voluntary Service of Armenia (HUJ) was founded in 1965 and is situated in the center of Yerevan. HUJ is a member of the Coordinating Committee of International Voluntary Service (CCIVS) at UNESCO and the Alliance of European Voluntary Service Organisations. The volunteer will assist in HUJ activities and promotion of volunteering lifestyle, in organization of international voluntary activities, promotion of HUJ volunteering projects. The participant will learn the aspects of a work in a voluntary service organisation's office, how to organize international voluntary workcamps, seminars/trainings, details of a work with long-term volunteers. After finishing the project, HUJ will help the volunteer to find a job in a voluntary service organisation. The volunteer will also have Armenian language classes in a language center twice a week, located not far from the office of HUJ. The volunteer will always find here a friendly atmosphere. Duration of the project is 8-12 months.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by HUJ Voluntary Service of Armenia in Yerevan, Armenia; activity period 52 weeks within 1 December 2026 – 30 November 2027. Themes: education and training. Application deadline: 30 November 2026. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 26 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: The volunteers will be provided with convenient accommodation: the dormitory of a university in Yerevan, near the city center, featuring same-gendered rooms with two occupants each, shared bathroom, and a spacious kitchen. This cozy dormitory is equipped with all necessities and ensures safety. Approximately 18 long-term ESC volunteers from different European countries reside in the dormitory. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
You will be working 30 - 35 hours per week. The main work will be in kitchen of seminar house or café and houskeeping, helping with the running of our seminar house for up to 150 guests during an event and working in the organic café, which is a meeting place for hikers and local tourists as well as seminar guests and community members. It’s open only on saturday and sunday during summertime. On the other days, our honor-system kiosk is open. Some hours you will work in garden or park. If you have sufficient German language skills, you can also work in guest services. The exact area in which you will work depends on your language skills, your personal preference and the needs in our community. Two hours per week you take time for your personal project and one is for mentoring.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by Projekt-Lebensbogen e.V. in Zierenberg, Germany; activity period 1 March 2027 – 28 February 2028. Themes: environment and nature and education and training. No fixed deadline: the host recruits on a rolling basis while the placement is open on the portal. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 26 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: We eat organic and mostly vegetarian and vegan food. When we eat together there is always a vegan option available. As a volunteer you have your own room with en-suite bathroom. You share the kitchen, living room, garden and other facilities with the community. And there is a music studio and a yoga and meditation space, that can be used by everyone. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

The volunteers will be part of the team of volunteers at the Salesian Youth Center Celje. Priorities that volunteers will carry out activities within the youth center itself - assistance and socializing on the playground and in club rooms, work with children and youth, preparation and implementation of activities with children and youth - playing board games, sports activities. Also, during the winter holidays when organizing various activities for the visitor center- both the daily program during the school year and the initial program during the summer holidays. In addition to working with children and young people who visit the center, the volunteers come together and work with a home team of volunteers who come to the center.
